channel.title: Axionalytics
channel.description: Architecture writing on enterprise agentic AI: deployment topology, execution isolation, human approval gates, data provenance, and analytics governance.

item.title: Why Enterprise AI Pilots Die in Security Review
item.description: The pilot worked. Eighteen months later it still is not in production. Five architectural questions decide that outcome, and all five are settled before the first line of code.

item.title: Prompt Injection Is a Containment Problem, Not a Prompting Problem
item.description: The defence and the attack share a channel, so no instruction closes the class. Four named attacks, and the architectural layers that make a successful one harmless.

item.title: Outbound Broke Because Volume Got Cheap
item.description: Research and volume trade against each other, and every team eventually picks the losing side. The way out is to automate the research and leave the send alone.

item.title: Your Sending Domain Is an Asset. Bounces Are How You Spend It.
item.description: Guessed addresses cost more than the campaign that produced them. Three escalating verification tiers, and the design decision that matters most when none of them can answer.

item.title: BYOC, SaaS, or On-Premises: Choosing a Deployment Topology for Enterprise AI
item.description: Deployment topology is not an infrastructure detail you settle later. It determines which data the system may touch, and it is the hardest decision to reverse.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop That Actually Holds: Write Gates, Blast Radius, and Replay Protection
item.description: Most human-in-the-loop is a confirmation dialog. Three properties separate a real approval gate from a checkbox that manufactures consent.

item.title: How an Agent Queries a 50,000-Table Warehouse Without Reading the Schema
item.description: Every demo works against twelve tables. Real catalogs have tens of thousands, and the standard approach collapses on cost, latency, and accuracy at the same time.

item.title: Requirements Traceability Without the Spreadsheet
item.description: The traceability matrix is accurate the day it is written and wrong within a sprint. Generating the link at authoring time is what makes it survive.

item.title: Line Coverage Is Not Verification Coverage
item.description: Most organisations can report line coverage to two decimals and cannot say which implemented behaviour nobody has written a test for. Those are different numbers.

item.title: Paying Down Legacy Test Debt Without an Engineer-Year
item.description: The assertions in a decade-old suite are usually fine. What is missing is everything around them — and retrofitting that is tractable in a way rewriting is not.

item.title: Your BI Backlog Is a Transcription Bottleneck, Not a Capacity Problem
item.description: Adding analysts to a forty-item queue buys a quarter of relief. The queue is long because the same dashboard is being hand-built for the eleventh time.

item.title: Excel Sprawl vs a Governed Semantic Model
item.description: The question is not which tool is better. It is which numbers the board sees when four departments each maintain their own version of revenue.

item.title: Building the Business Case for Enterprise AI
item.description: Finance rejects AI business cases for predictable reasons. Understated loaded cost, unfalsifiable benefits, and an automation rate nobody believes.

item.title: Why Enterprise Dashboards Get Abandoned
item.description: A dashboard nobody opens is not a design failure. It is a specification failure — it was built from the data that existed rather than the decision it serves.

item.title: Build, Buy, or Assemble: Sourcing Enterprise AI Capability
item.description: The build-versus-buy framing hides the option most enterprises actually need, and the three constraints that decide it have nothing to do with engineering capacity.
